local_articles.title: Swimming prodigy Yu Zidi, 13, says ‘interviews way harder than racing’
local_articles.snippet: TOKYO – The 13-year-old Chinese swimmer Yu Zidi has taken the Asian Games by storm, but when it comes to the intense interest in her, she said: “Interviews are way harder than the race.” Yu smashed the Games record in winning the women’s 200m butterfly on Sept 20 in Tokyo and then repeated the feat in the Sept 21 200m individual medley. The schoolgirl’s 2min 6.10sec in scorching to victory in the medley was the fastest time in the world in 2026. She was only 0.4 seconds off the world record held by Canada’s Summer McIntosh. Yu has been the talk of swimming since becoming the youngest medallist in world championships history in 2025 with bronze for China’s relay team aged just 12. She is shaping up to be a major medal threat at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics. questions.title: Which activist detained in Tunisia's Global Sumud Flotilla fundraising case will suspend his hunger strike between September 12 and September 27, 2026?
questions.background: Four activists have been detained since March in a Tunisian investigation into alleged financial irregularities involving fundraising for the Global Sumud Flotilla, an international campaign seeking to deliver aid to Gaza. Hunger strikes are being used to protest their continued detention.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Contemporaneous reporting by Al Jazeera identifying which of the four detained activists has suspended his hunger strike. Resolution Conditions : The suspension must have occurred between September 12 and September 27, 2026, inclusive. Appeals to suspend the strike or statements of future intention do not count. Accepted Answer Format : The activist's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-09-20 update (Al Jazeera Sept 20 — explicit Source of Truth — and Roots TV Sept 18): Al Jazeera's Tunis report today confirms NONE of the four detained Global Sumud Flotilla activists has suspended his hunger strike yet following Saturday's Tunis solidarity protest ('remain determined to continue their hunger strike until their release'). Crucially, Al Jazeera reports Wael Naouar has now reached ~35 days on hunger strike (since Aug 16), suffering repeated fainting, difficulty breathing, hallucinations, and >20kg (44lb) weight loss ('real danger threatening him'), whereas the other three only joined on Sept 9 (~Day 11 today, 24 days behind Naouar; Henchiri still urgently needs surgery for a prior injury in Israel, keeping him clear #2).
